context: Tests the When Not to Use boundary: the skill is for non-technical readers, not engineers.

checklist.name: Identifies the audience as engineers
checklist.description: The response states that the readers are platform engineers who already know the terminology.

checklist.name: Recognises plain English is not the right fit
checklist.description: The response says the plain English translation style is meant for non-technical stakeholders and is not needed for this audience.

checklist.name: Keeps technical terms
checklist.description: Kubernetes and service mesh terms are not replaced with everyday substitutes.

checklist.name: Keeps exact configuration values
checklist.description: The configuration values are preserved unchanged.

checklist.name: Does not rewrite for executives
checklist.description: The response does not restructure the doc into an executive summary with business impact framing.

checklist.name: May offer selective translation
checklist.description: If it offers any simplification, it limits this to selective translation for mixed audiences and keeps technical depth for the peer review.

checklist.name: Does not add an unrequested glossary
checklist.description: The response does not add a glossary of terms the reviewers already know.

checklist.name: Wording tidy-up is still done
checklist.description: The response still improves clarity of wording (for example concise sentences or active voice) without changing technical content.

checklist.name: Explains the choice briefly
checklist.description: The response gives a short reason for how it handled the style request.

checklist.name: Produces or describes the edited design.md
checklist.description: `design.md` is edited, or the response describes the specific wording changes made.
